goal: Establish a constrained Goose-to-C-to-CUDA device function path and compare CUDA call overhead from AOT Goose and C++; no production integration.
kernel: FP32 SiLU-gate, pure scalar function written in Goose; restricted generated-C device translation; native CUDA math/order reference.
scope: The generated device function must not call Goose runtime, allocate, use TLS, or retain CPU pointers. This is a custom restricted path, not an upstream CUDA backend. C ABI bridge launches/owns CUDA resources.
protocol: Build/check first, then correctness over representative dimensions/tails/extremes and CUDA memcheck; sequential native and Goose host launch loops with identical shared CUDA bridge and paired order. No model requests or speedup claims for full Apex.
acceptance: Record toolchain/build success, actual device execution and max errors. Report both host enqueue/full synchronized time and GPU event time. Any launch overhead claim is local to the fixed probe. No default switch.
